response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. The fields are joined with '_' and not escaped. Resource names and folder UIDs can contain '_'. For example, name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" produce the same key. Check writes this key with permDenialCache.Set whenever a request is denied. It reads the key first and returns Allowed:false on any hit, before it looks at permissions. A denial for one resource can therefore be served as a denial for a different resource of the same user and action.
response.title: Denial cache key joins fields with an unescaped '_', so different (name, folder) pairs can share a key
